title: The Mileage Interval a Completed Inspection Grants a Keyturn Vehicle Listing
content:
A completed inspection of a Keyturn Vehicle Listing grants the vehicle a mileage interval, and how many miles it grants is worked out before the inspection is filed. A completed inspection grants a mileage interval worked out from the standard interval of 10000 miles, adjusted for what the vehicle's own record shows and finally held to a floor of 1000 miles.

The standard interval is 10000 miles, and the whole of it is open to a vehicle whose own record calls for nothing further.

The additions and reductions the vehicle's record calls for are summed and applied once to the standard interval, rather than each being applied to the figure the one before it produced, and the figure so reached is a whole number of miles.

The interval reached is finally compared with the floor of 1000 miles and the greater of the two is the interval the inspection grants, expressed as a whole number of miles.

### Worked through on hypothetical records

*A vehicle whose record calls for nothing further.* The standard interval of 10000 miles is the interval reached; compared with the floor of 1000 miles the greater of the two is 10000, and the inspection grants 10000 miles.

*A vehicle whose record calls for additions of 1200 and 1600 miles and reductions of 800 and 3200 miles.* The four are summed to a net reduction of 1200 miles, and that net is applied once to the standard interval of 10000 miles, giving 8800 miles. Compared with the floor of 1000 miles the greater of the two is 8800, and the inspection grants 8800 miles. Had each figure instead been laid on the figure the one before it produced, the same four would still give 8800 miles, because they are summed and applied once whatever their order.

*A vehicle whose record leaves the interval at 600 miles.* Compared with the floor of 1000 miles the greater of the two is 1000, and the inspection grants 1000 miles.
